q: A one-dimensional array A[-5..20] is stored in memory with base address 1000 and each element occupies 4 bytes. What is the address of A[8]?
Evaluate the postfix expression: 5 6 2 + * 12 4 / -
A circular queue is implemented in an array of size 6 (indices 0 to 5). Front = 4 and rear = 1, where rear is the index of the last inserted element. How many elements are in the queue?
exp: Count = (rear - front + size) mod size + 1 = (1 - 4 + 6) mod 6 + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4 (elements at indices 4, 5, 0, 1).

q: In a singly linked list that has only a head pointer, which of the following operations takes O(n) time?
options: Inserting a node at the beginning
Checking whether the list is empty
exp: To delete the last node we must traverse to the second last node, which needs O(n) time; the other operations are O(1).

q: A full binary tree (every node has 0 or 2 children) has 5 internal nodes. What is the total number of nodes in the tree?
exp: In a full binary tree, leaves = internal nodes + 1 = 6, so total = 5 + 6 = 11.

q:
Statement I: Depth First Search of a graph can be implemented using a stack.
Statement II: Breadth First Search finds the shortest path (fewest edges) from the source in an unweighted graph.
Which option is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
exp: DFS uses an explicit or recursion stack, and BFS explores vertices level by level, so it gives fewest-edge paths.

q: A hash table of size 7 uses h(k) = k mod 7 with linear probing. Keys 15, 22, 8 and 29 are inserted in this order. In which slot does 29 finally get stored?
exp: All four keys hash to slot 1. 15 goes to 1, 22 to 2, 8 to 3 and 29 to 4.

q: How many swaps does bubble sort perform to sort the array 5 4 3 2 1 into ascending order?
exp: Each swap removes exactly one inversion. The reversed array of 5 elements has 5×4/2 = 10 inversions, so 10 swaps.

q: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching for a key in a binary search tree of n nodes that has become completely skewed?
exp: A skewed BST degenerates into a linked list of height n-1, so search may visit all n nodes.

q: A two-dimensional array A[1..4][1..5] is stored in column-major order with base address 200 and element size 2 bytes. What is the address of A[3][4]?
exp: Offset = ((4-1)×4 + (3-1)) × 2 = 14 × 2 = 28, so address = 228. (226 would be the row-major address.)

q: The postfix form of the infix expression (A+B)*C-D/E is
exp: (A+B) gives AB+; times C gives AB+C*; D/E gives DE/; subtraction gives AB+C*DE/-.

q: A queue is initially empty. The operations performed are: enqueue(1), enqueue(2), enqueue(3), dequeue, enqueue(4), dequeue, enqueue(5). Which element is now at the front?
exp: After enqueues 1,2,3 and a dequeue the queue is 2,3; add 4 then dequeue removes 2 giving 3,4; adding 5 gives 3,4,5. Front is 3.

q: Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm detects a cycle in a linked list. What is its auxiliary space complexity?
exp: It uses only two pointers (slow and fast), so extra space is constant.

q: The preorder traversal of a binary tree is A B D E C F and the inorder traversal is D B E A F C. What is its postorder traversal?
options: D E B C F A
D B E F C A
D E B F C A
F D E B C A
exp: A is the root; B(D,E) is the left subtree and C with left child F is the right subtree. Postorder = D E B F C A.

q: Selection sort is used to sort 10 elements. Exactly how many comparisons does it make?
exp: Selection sort always does (n-1)+(n-2)+...+1 = n(n-1)/2 = 45 comparisons.

q: A hash table with 10 slots uses chaining and h(k) = k mod 10. Keys 12, 22, 32, 15, 25 and 7 are inserted. What is the length of the longest chain?
exp: 12, 22 and 32 all hash to slot 2 giving a chain of 3; slot 5 has 2 keys and slot 7 has 1.

q: Keys 10, 20, 15, 30, 40 are inserted one by one into an initially empty max-heap (stored in an array, using standard sift-up). What is the final array?
In a B-tree of order 5 (maximum 5 children per node), what is the minimum number of keys in a non-root internal node?
exp: Minimum children = ceil(5/2) = 3, so minimum keys = 3 - 1 = 2.

q: An array A[-3..4][2..6] has how many elements?
Evaluate the prefix expression: - * + 4 3 2 5
exp: Scanning from the right: 4+3=7; 7*2=14; 14-5=9.

q: Which of the following is NOT an application of a queue?
exp: Postfix evaluation uses a stack; the others use FIFO queues.

q: A weighted undirected graph has edges: A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10, D-E 2, D-F 6, E-F 3. What is the weight of its minimum spanning tree?
exp: Kruskal picks B-C(1), A-C(2), D-E(2), E-F(3), skips A-B (cycle), picks B-D(5): 1+2+2+3+5 = 13.

q: What is the minimum number of moves required to solve the Tower of Hanoi puzzle with 5 disks?
exp: Minimum moves = 2ⁿ - 1 = 2⁵ - 1 = 31.

q: What is the time complexity of building a binary heap from n unordered elements using the bottom-up (Floyd) method?
exp: Most nodes are near the leaves and sift down only a few levels, so the total work sums to O(n).

q: What is the minimum number of nodes in an AVL tree of height 4? (Height of a single-node tree is 0.)
An undirected graph has 8 vertices and 11 edges. How many entries equal 1 in its adjacency matrix?
exp: Each undirected edge sets two entries (A[i][j] and A[j][i]), so 2 × 11 = 22.

q: Insertion sort is applied to the array 7 3 5 1. What does the array look like after the first two insertions (the first two passes)?
exp: Pass 1 inserts 3 giving 3 7 5 1; pass 2 inserts 5 giving 3 5 7 1.

q: Which statement correctly gives the time and extra space needed to reverse a singly linked list of n nodes iteratively?
options: O(n) time and O(n) extra space
O(n) time and O(1) extra space
O(n²) time and O(1) extra space
O(log n) time and O(1) extra space
exp: One pass changes each node's next pointer using three pointers, so it is O(n) time and O(1) space.

q: A hash table of size 50 currently stores 35 keys. What is its load factor?
exp: Load factor α = number of keys / table size = 35/50 = 0.7.

q: A 6 × 6 lower triangular matrix is stored in a one-dimensional array keeping only the elements on and below the diagonal. How many elements are stored?
Integers 1, 2, 3, 4 are pushed onto a stack in this order, with pops allowed at any time between pushes. Which of the following pop sequences is NOT possible?
exp: Once 3 is popped the stack holds 1 below 2, so 2 must be popped before 1. The sequence 3 1 2 4 violates this.

q: What is the maximum number of comparisons needed by binary search to find a key in a sorted array of 1000 elements?
exp: Maximum comparisons = floor(log₂ 1000) + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10.

q: The keys 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 35 are inserted in this order into an empty BST. What is the height of the tree (counted in edges)?
exp: The path 50 -> 30 -> 40 -> 35 has 3 edges and is the longest.

q: A directed graph has adjacency lists 1:{2,3}, 2:{4}, 3:{4}, 4:{}. Depth first search starts at vertex 1 and visits neighbours in ascending order. What is the visiting order?
exp: From 1 go to 2, then 4, backtrack to 1 and visit 3 (4 already visited).

q: A circular queue is implemented in an array of size 8 using the convention that the queue is full when (rear + 1) mod 8 = front. What is the maximum number of elements it can hold?
exp: One slot is left unused to distinguish full from empty, so capacity is 8 - 1 = 7.

q:
What is returned by f(4825)?
int f(int x){ if(x==0) return 0; return x%10 + f(x/10); }
exp: It sums the digits: 5 + 2 + 8 + 4 = 19.

q: The array 4 10 3 5 1 is converted into a max-heap using the bottom-up heapify method. What is the resulting array?
exp: Heapify 10 (fine); heapify 4: swap with 10 giving 10 4 3 5 1, then 4 swaps with 5 giving 10 5 3 4 1.

q: A hash table of size 7 uses double hashing with h1(k) = k mod 7 and h2(k) = 5 - (k mod 5), and probe i position (h1 + i·h2) mod 7. Key 10 is inserted first, then key 17. In which slot is 17 placed?
exp: 10 goes to slot 3. For 17: h1=3 (occupied), h2 = 5-2 = 3, so next slot = (3+3) mod 7 = 6.

q: The running time of an algorithm satisfies T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n. Which is its complexity?
exp: By the master theorem a=2, b=2, f(n)=n = n^(log₂2), giving Θ(n log n).
